title: Tin Yan Rachel Lee
text:
Hi everyone! I came from Hong Kong and had been living in Toronto for four years before MDS. Through my work in education marketing and healthcare advocacy, I have seen how data can shape decisions which cause significant social and business impact. In this program, I would like to learn more about how to use data to make predictions which drive informed decisions. Apart from work and learning, I love hiking and tennis:)

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
The first week of MDS has been both exciting and challenging. Being a student again after a few years of working feels quite different, and I’m trying my best to adjust to the student schedule and rebuild my learning habits. In the prerequisite courses, we had already covered some of the concepts introduced in the first week, so we were not completely overwhelmed. However, starting from the second week, new knowledge has been coming at us quickly! Discipline and persistence will definitely be our best friends throughout the program.
As mentioned, the pace of MDS is very fast, so time management is an important skill for succeeding in the program. Outside of studying, I also think it is crucial to set aside time for both our physical and mental well-being, as well as for the people we care about. It is definitely easier said than done, but over these 10 months, I will try to remind myself from time to time to maintain a healthy balance between school and life.
Here is a picture I took at Deep Cove during the long weekend. I also managed to squeeze in a short hike!



Nice day out at Deep Cove.

In this post, we would explore the different in mass in the penguins considering their gender and species.

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

Before the analysis, the data must be cleaned. Observations containing missing values are dropped.

clean_penguins <- penguins |> 
  drop_na()

clean_penguins

Next, we would like to confirm if there is a mass difference between male and female penguins in general among the three species.

mass_difference <- clean_penguins |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g))

Last but not least, we create a boxplot to compare the mass between the three species. According to the figure, Gentoo is significant heavier than the other two species. The average mass of Adelie and Chinstrap are similar but the distribution of mass of Adelie is greater.

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot()

title: About

Background
I grew up and studied in Hong Kong, where I earned my undergraduate degree in Sociology from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, with a minor in Journalism and Communication. I began my career in marketing and communications, working across education, financial services, and healthcare in both Hong Kong and Canada.

title: About
text:
Why data science
Through these experiences, particularly my work in healthcare advocacy, I became increasingly interested in how data can be used to understand complex problems, guide decisions, and create meaningful social impact. This interest ultimately led me to pursue graduate studies in Data Science and build toward a career applying analytics to real-world challenges.

title: About
text:
Outside of data science
Outside of work and study, I love spending time outdoors, especially hiking. That is one of the reasons I enjoy living in Vancouver, being surrounded by mountains, forests and beautiful scenery makes it easy to escape into nature whenever I have the chance. I also love trying different food and Mexican food is definitely one of my favourites! If there is a hike to join or tacos involved, count me in!
